text:
ashwin: Quick context — saw a perf regression on Dedicated last night after the kernel-selection change. p95 up ~18%. I ran a tiny nsys micro-trace and noticed a lot of kernel-switch churn around the kv_cache_lookup + decoder kernels. Need a safe, low-overhead profiling approach we can run in-prod to collect more signal without blowing SLOs. Thoughts?

maria: Can you paste the short nsys summary you grabbed? even 5 lines helps. Also which pool/region and model?

ashwin: us-west-2 dedicated pool, redis-backed KV cache, llama-variant. Quick snippet from the nsys short output I captured:

```
GPU activity: kernel_switch (20ms), kv_cache_lookup (45ms), fused_attention_fp16 (120ms)
CPU activity: host memcpy (12ms), nvlink sync (8ms)
Overall snapshot duration: 350ms (but we aborted after 3 tokens)
```

noah: OK. Two pragmatic ideas: (1) continuous micro-probes — extremely short nsys snapshots sampled at ~0.1% of requests that only collect kernel timeline aggregates, not full memory dumps; (2) on-demand full snapshots triggered when the micro-probe metric exceeds a threshold (e.g., kernel_switch_count per request > X). That keeps duty-cycle tiny.

kelly: Add guardrails: auto-disable probes if we see >1% increase in p50 for the traced hosts over a 10m window, and cap total per-host trace time to e.g., 30s/day. Also TTL traces so they stop if queueing/latency spikes.

ashwin: Agree. Curious about KV cache behaviour — could cache misses cause extra kernel-switch churn? If so we should correlate probe hits with cache hit/miss tag in the trace. Need to avoid logging tokens or prompts.

maria: We can avoid sensitive data by tagging only metadata flags (cache_hit: true/false, kernel_switch_count: N, seq_len: L). Emit those as metrics to graphite/prometheus from the probe wrapper; no raw strings.

infra-ci-bot: Deploy scheduled: feature-flag "microprobe-sentinel" will be rolled to canary fleet in us-west-2 at 03:00 UTC. CI pipeline will attach minimal-trace binary.

noah: Implementation sketch (pseudo):

```bash
# enabled by flag + env vars, very short capture window
TRACE_MICRO_PROBE=1 SAMPLE_RATE=0.005 MAX_SNAPSHOTS=2 
  /opt/redwood/bin/runtime --trace-mode=nsys-short --trace-max-ms=200 \
  --emit-metrics="kernel_switch_count,kv_cache_hit"

# trigger full snapshot if kernel_switch_count > 4 in a microtrace
```

kelly: Rollout plan I recommend: night-window 0.5% traffic for 24h -> compare to baseline; if stable, open to 2% daytime for 48h; enable full-snapshot triggers only after microprobe baseline is validated. Document an abort checklist and phasing.

ashwin: Also propose a lightweight internal metric in runtime: increment kernel_switch_count per request and expose as tag on existing latency histogram. That lets us do cohort comparison without any tracing. If we see weird cohorts, then flip the microprobe trigger on for those cohorts.

sre-bot: Security note: traces must be scrubbed via the redwood-trace-redactor: remove prompt tokens, user IDs, and IPs. Also run traces only in clusters with logging retention set to <30d for team review.

ashwin: Great. Action items: (1) noah + maria: build microprobe wrapper + metric emission (2) kelly: write rollout + abort checklist (3) infra: feature-flag canary at 03:00 UTC (4) ops: add Prom alert when traced-host p50 delta > 1%. I'll post a short runbook after we have the wrapper.

maria: I'll sketch the prometheus labels we'll use: cluster, host_id, probe_version, cache_hit, kernel_switch_count, seq_len, model_version.

noah: I'll prototype the nsys-short wrapper today and push a test image to staging. keeping sample_rate low by default.

kelly: I'll draft the rollback steps and include the latency gating rule for automation.

ashwin: Thanks all. If anyone wants to pair on the redaction rules, ping me.
